title: End to End Projects With AI: A Strict, Verifiable Workflow

cover.alt: Conceptual workbench illustration of an AI-assisted build assembled and checked by a human.

figures.title: What AI drafts, and what the builder verifies
figures.summary: The same task has two responsibilities: producing a starting point and proving that it works.

items.label: Structure
items.detail: AI proposes folders and scaffolding; the builder checks that the layout is understandable.

items.label: Logic
items.detail: AI drafts behavior; the builder tests real inputs and edge cases.

items.label: Debugging
items.detail: AI suggests fixes from supplied errors; the builder examines logs and runtime behavior.

items.label: Deployment
items.detail: AI drafts configuration; the builder runs the build and checks the live system.

figures.caption: A responsibility comparison from the article. A plausible draft is not evidence of a working system.

figures.title: The runnable-slice loop
figures.summary: Each cycle ends with observed behavior rather than the amount of generated code.

items.label: Describe
items.detail: State one concrete behavior in plain language.

items.label: Draft
items.detail: Create a small entry point, route, page, or rendering slice.

items.label: Run and inspect
items.detail: Reproduce the failure and read the actual output.

items.label: Change one thing
items.detail: Apply a narrow fix and rerun the local system.

items.label: Deploy and verify
items.detail: Repeat the checks in the live environment.

items.label: Document
items.detail: Record the working path before the next iteration.
